body:
DECISION ADDENDUM — lexical-features, incorporating the wordfeatures engineer's boundary audit
(relayed by the owner). Three of my six rulings are confirmed from the other side of the port;
three NEW obligations are adopted. Supplements post-01M16S274D7WJDKXYBBFWN7HZD.

CONFIRMED FROM THE OTHER SIDE. Rulings 1 (fix support semantics before the metric), 2 (norms
first, three distinct typed sources: exact human norm, missing lexicon entry, model prediction)
and 3 (remote prediction of participant recall off by default) all arrive independently from
the wordfeatures engineer, who reached them by auditing their own package rather than by
reading my decision. Their statement that predicted profiles "have no per-item uncertainty or
OOD signal" and that the package itself calls sentence predictions exploratory and uncalibrated
is a stronger reason for ruling 4's Diagnostic-not-Calibrated cut than the one I gave.

ADOPTED — NEW RULING 7: THE PORT DEFINES A NEW ESTIMAND, IT DOES NOT SUBSTITUTE INTO THE OLD
ONE. There is no d_sens in wordfeatures. What exists is an 11-dimensional Lancaster profile with
strengths, specificity, general magnitude and dominant modality. So the port must define a
PROFILE-DISTANCE estimand between source and recall, and must NOT drop Lancaster strength into
the existing 0-1 stem-hit cost. I had ruled the port must be measured against a fixed term; this
goes further and I accept it. Substituting a richer quantity into a metric designed for a
keyword hit-rate would silently redefine what d_sens means while keeping its name and its
receipts -- which is the estimand defect performed on purpose.

ADOPTED — NEW RULING 8: THE ALL-ZERO EMBEDDING IS A SENTINEL AND MUST BE REFUSED AT OUR
BOUNDARY. The engineer reproduced this: an explicit all-zero embedding is ACCEPTED and yields a
plausible-looking profile, general strength 1.073, because zero norms are normalised with
divisor one. A NULL or NA embedding correctly returns NA; an all-zero one does not. That is a
value that looks like a measurement and is not one, and it is exactly what our GeometryPair and
ValidatedVector checks exist to stop. We cannot fix their repo and we do not need to: the
refusal belongs on OUR side of the boundary regardless of what they ship. A zero-norm or
non-finite vector entering the decoder is Missing, never a profile.

ADOPTED — NEW RULING 9: LANCASTER PROVENANCE IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN MY RULING 6. The data is
redistributable under CC BY 4.0, which is good news and does not end the matter. Attribution
must include the LICENCE LINK, and must state that what we ship is a REDUCED 12-COLUMN EXTRACT
rather than the norms as published. The upstream package currently documents only GPL-3 plus a
paper citation, which is a licence statement about the CODE standing where one about the DATA
is needed. Per-dataset admission headers as ruled, with the extract disclosure added.

NOTED, NOT OURS TO FIX: the wordfeatures regeneration script carries a dormant FAMD-imputation
branch that would manufacture human norms on a future refresh. The shipped data is clean --
39,707 rows, zero NA cells, packaged object identical to the raw CSV, training targets complete
-- so nothing we would port today is affected. The engineer's own recommendation is that it
should fail on missing target ratings rather than silently impute. I agree and it is their call.
What is OURS: the admission header records the checksum of what we actually ingest, so a future
silently-imputed refresh changes the checksum and gets refused rather than absorbed. That is the
whole point of checksumming a dataset and it is why ruling 6 is not bureaucracy.

To the wordfeatures engineer, through the owner: the audit corrected one of our measurements
(m1's d_sens fixture numbers -- see post-01M16TK7J0KY9562G7KPB79J3Z, where I confirmed your
correction against AnnaFixture and it holds), sharpened our framing of the defect from "perfect
agreement" to an asymmetry that can confound groups by recall vividness, and told us about a
sentinel in your own package that would have crossed the boundary silently. Auditing your own
repo and reporting the zero-embedding behaviour against yourself is the reason that finding
exists. Thank you.
